beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Rights Are Not Real asks why a recognized entitlement can fail to protect someone.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The provocative title separates moral claims, legal recognition, and institutions that make protection effective.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The book first gives political power its strongest realistic hearing.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: It then challenges the mistake of treating successful coercion as moral justification.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Readers follow that tension toward protections strong enough to restrain their own defenders.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: A moral claim can remain meaningful even when a legal system refuses to recognize it.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Legal recognition can exist while practical enforcement remains weak or inaccessible.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Effective protection depends on coordinated institutions and people able to make violation costly.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The book separates these layers because their familiar combination can hide the work sustaining them.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Its title challenges complacency about protection, not the possibility of judging existing power morally.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The argument first examines organization, coercion, institutional capture, and the costs of sustained vigilance.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: It then confronts the slide from explaining power to declaring its outcomes legitimate.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: A durable institution needs information and criticism that unrestricted authority can destroy.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The proposed counterpower protects people while limiting those entrusted with their defense.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: This movement makes the book more demanding than a simple celebration of political realism.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Begin with the three meanings of a right and preserve their differences throughout the argument.
